title: Is my shop as busy as my graph says? Node.js cluster metrics, counted two ways
description: otel-cluster-metrics against the stock exporter, same app, same traffic.

options.content:
## Is my shop as busy as my graph says?
Not with the usual setup. This is one small online shop, run twice with exactly the same visitors. **Blue** counts the whole shop in one place, with [otel-cluster-metrics](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics). **Orange** is the usual setup: each of the shop's four workers keeps its own count, and the graph only hears from one of them at a time. Every four minutes one worker is swapped for a new one, the way real servers restart.

panels.title: The usual setup reports
panels.description: Requests a second as the usual setup reports them, divided by the real count from the whole-shop endpoint, over the last hour. The right answer is 1×.

panels.title: Requests a second: same visitors, two counts
panels.description: Both shops get exactly the same visitors, so the lines should sit on top of each other. Orange runs high because every time its count falls, Prometheus reads the fall as a restart and adds the count again. Violet bars mark each worker swap.

targets.legendFormat: one count for the whole shop
usual setup, one count per worker

targets.expr: count by (worker) (label_replace((max by (cluster_worker_id) (worker_heap_used{job="shop-api"}) unless max by (cluster_worker_id) (worker_heap_used{job="shop-api"} offset $__interval)) and on () count(max by (cluster_worker_id) (worker_heap_used{job="shop-api"} offset $__interval)), "worker", "$1", "cluster_worker_id", "([0-9]+):.*"))

matcher.options: one count for the whole shop
usual setup, one count per worker
^worker .* starts$

panels.title: Times the count started over, last hour
panels.description: A request count should only go up. Each time it falls, Prometheus assumes the app restarted and guesses the missing part. The whole-shop count never falls. The usual setup falls hundreds of times an hour: at each worker swap, and each time a different worker answers.

options.content:
**shop-api** (blue) uses [@adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics): workers report to the primary, which serves one `/metrics` for the whole cluster. **shop-api-stock** (orange) runs the stock OpenTelemetry Prometheus exporter in each worker on the shared port, so each scrape reaches whichever worker accepts it. Every four minutes one worker is retired and replaced, one in five times with SIGKILL.

An OpenTelemetry Collector scrapes both `/metrics` endpoints every 15 seconds and sends them to Grafana Cloud over OTLP. A load generator sends the same requests to both clusters, on a one-hour wave between about 5 and 25 requests a second.

- Package: [@adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics), source on [GitHub](https://github.com/adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics)
- Run this dashboard yourself: [examples/grafana](https://github.com/adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics/tree/main/examples/grafana) (`docker compose up`, then open Grafana on port 3000)
- Dashboard JSON with a data source picker: [dashboard.json](https://github.com/adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics/blob/main/examples/grafana/dashboard.json)
